correctness.rationale: Exactly one deletion followed by standardization gives a set D(p) of distinct four-permutation outputs; single-deletion correction is exactly pairwise disjointness of these sets, even when a word's own outputs repeat. The increasing-index enumeration visits each admissible set once and cannot discard an admissible branch on the candidate-shortfall test. The independent replay (branches/ef0d61bf-8c7a-4831-a402-809fe629a222/replay_s5.py and replay_output.txt) independently rebuilt outputs, found 1568 eight-sets and zero nine-sets, so no larger code exists either. Position reversal and value complement commute with relabeling the survivors; inversion transposes the matrix and exchanges the omitted row and column, deriving the inverse standardized output. The first two involutions commute and inversion swaps them, giving the eight transformations of the action. The replay recovered 220 orbits with counts 2,1,43,174 at sizes 1,2,4,8, and 36 sets avoid both monotones. It also enumerated the 25 ascent/inverse-ascent weighted residue classes modulo five, finding the displayed eight-word set as the unique largest class. The supplied verifiers were inspected, not executed; this is finite exhaustive evidence, not formal or expert certification.

value.rationale: The exact small fixed-length optimum tests the established asymptotic construction in a natural benchmark with 120 possible words and a nontrivial confusability graph. The full equality classification shows that the construction is far from unique even modulo the natural symmetries, and that including a monotone word is not necessary for optimality. The census answers a meaningful structural question not resolved by producing one code.
